title: Split scheduler loop and modularize KV cache lifecycle to reduce mutex contention
creator: Aisha Fernandez
description:
Summary: This ticket refactors the serving runtime's scheduler and KV cache lifecycle to remove a central mutex hotspot that increases tail latency under high concurrent streams. We will split the monolithic scheduler loop into two cooperating loops (fast-path request dispatch + slower maintenance loop) and extract KV cache lifecycle (warmup, eviction, compaction) into a modular controller with pluggable policies.

Why: Current end-to-end measurements show a global scheduler mutex held across batching and KV cache touch paths. Under bursty traffic the mutex causes priority inversion and 95/99th latency spikes. Separating hot paths from maintenance work and modularizing cache lifecycle will reduce contention and make future policy changes safe to iterate.

Scope:
- Introduce scheduler split: dispatch loop (per-core, lock-free fast-path) + maintenance loop (per-node, batch coordination, metrics aggregation).
- Replace the global batcher mutex with a sharded ring buffer + per-shard atomic state and optional spin hint.
- Implement KV lifecycle controller that runs eviction/compaction as background jobs with quotas and backpressure signals to the dispatch loop.
- Add metrics and tracing hooks to validate handoff and backpressure paths.
- Upgrade runtime deps: tokio 1.28.0, tonic 0.9.x, prost 0.11.x, bump prometheus client to 0.15.x.

Non-goals: Full rewrite of batch lane scheduling (will be follow-up). End-to-end feature changes to API surface.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit and integration tests for scheduler split and KV controller exist.
- Benchmarks show >=12% throughput improvement or >=15% reduction in p99 latency on standard internal benchmark under 800 concurrent streams, compared to baseline.
- No regression on token correctness or cache hit semantics.
- CI green across Linux x86_64 and containerized smoke tests.

Notes on approach: We avoid introducing heavy-handed actor frameworks; prefer small modules that are easy to audit. The KV lifecycle controller exposes a minimal API: signal_eviction(reason), schedule_compaction(range), and stat_export(). The dispatch loop will observe per-shard token consumption counters to apply light-weight backpressure.
updates: 2025-11-04: Spike complete. Validated concept with micro-bench prototype (dispatch-only vs maintenance split) on devbox; measured 18% p99 reduction in toy workload for single-node run. - Aisha

2025-11-12: Design review with runtime team. Agreed on sharded ring buffer approach (8 shards per core by default) and on a single maintenance loop per node. Priya asked for clear metrics around handoff latency; added tracing spans. - Miguel

2025-11-20: Started implementation: created scheduler/split package, basic ring buffer and per-shard counters. WIP PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4321. Running unit tests locally; two flaky tests observed in batcher integration (timing). - Miguel

2025-11-28: Dependency upgrades prepared in a separate branch to isolate surface area: tokio/tonic/prost. Had to adapt tonic streaming API changes (server side) — small API shim added. Integration tests for gRPC streams passing locally. - Miguel

2025-12-02: Internal perf run (k8s staging): 12.3% throughput improvement and 18% p99 latency drop under 800 concurrent streams vs baseline. KV warmup still causes brief 10ms spikes at startup; added warmup quota to controller. Dashboard: grafana.redwood.internal/d/serving/scheduler-refactor-15903. - Aisha

2025-12-05: Code review feedback from Priya Kapoor and Sam Reynolds: address documentation of invariants, add more assertions around ring buffer full path, and add a feature flag to toggle new maintenance loop. Preparing PR updates. - Miguel
risk: Medium. Changes introduce new concurrency primitives and dependency bumps. The main risk is subtle ordering bugs in handoff between dispatch and maintenance loops that can surface as token loss or double-eviction. Mitigations: feature flag, extensive assertions in debug builds, and staged rollouts with canary traffic. If tokio bump exposes a hidden regression, we will revert the dependency bump branch independently.
testing_plan: 1) Unit tests for ring buffer, per-shard counters, and KV controller. 2) Integration tests with full batcher and streaming GRPC harness. 3) Perf benchmarks on staging k8s cluster (baseline vs new). 4) Gradual canary on production with: 1% -> 5% -> 25% traffic, validate p99, error rates, and prometheus metrics for handoff-latency. 5) Post-deploy synthetic load tests for 48h.
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag to disable maintenance loop and ring buffer; revert to previous single-loop scheduler commit if immediate toggle fails; if dependency upgrade is implicated, rollback dependency bump branch and cut a hotfix runtime-1.21 release containing only the revert. Documented rollback steps in the runbook.
notes: Design decision: prefer sharded, lock-avoidant structures over a single global mutex to improve scaling; this increases code paths to test but reduces future contention risk.
PR code owners: @miguel, @aisha, @priya. Need additional review from storage/KV owners for eviction semantics.
Follow-up: split batch-lane assignment logic into a separate ticket after this lands (low-risk incrementalization).
